summary.text: 床 is a popular graphic variant of 牀 that later became the standard form. The historical analysis of 牀 assigns 木 a meaning role and 爿 a sound role. An alternative account interprets 爿 as a picture of a bed, but its cited early use is glossed as a place name.

formation.text: The historical graph 牀 is analyzed as phonosemantic: 木 contributes meaning, while 爿 is assigned a phonetic role. A separate paleographic interpretation proposes that 爿 depicts a bed and was an early graph for it; the cited inscription is glossed as a place name, so this pictorial reading and the sequence between 爿 and 牀 remain uncertain.

components.text: In 牀, 木 is identified as the semantic element, linking the graph to resting furniture. It belongs to the historical graph, not the current form 床.
The traditional analysis assigns 爿 a phonetic role in 牀. A separate account interprets an oracle-bone form as a bed picture, but its cited inscription use is glossed as a place name.

sound_limitation.text: A secondary Zhengzhang report gives 爿 *zaŋ (also *braːn) and 床/牀 *zraŋ, a broadly similar comparison, but it has not been independently verified against the original source. The available evidence does not establish 爿’s pronunciation in its proposed role; Baxter–Sagart *k.dzraŋ is a reconstruction for the word written 牀, not an independent reconstruction of 爿.

sound.text: A secondary Zhengzhang phonetic-series table reports 爿 *zaŋ (also *braːn) beside 床/牀 *zraŋ in the same reconstruction system. The forms are broadly similar, but the report has not been independently verified against the original reconstruction source.
sound.system: Old Chinese, Zhengzhang (2003), as reported secondarily

history.text: 床 is recorded as a popular variant of 牀, and that popular form later became standard. This is a graphic variant relationship, not evidence that 床 is an earlier form.

The selected Warring States bronze-style redraw shows 牀 with 木 and 爿; the oracle-bone-style redraw shows 爿 alone. These illustrate forms discussed in historical accounts but do not establish a sequence of development; both are modern digital redrawings.

uncertainties.text: The proposal that oracle-bone 爿 depicts a bed remains uncertain: its cited inscription use is glossed as a place name, and the account does not date that inscription. The chronology between 爿 and 牀 is unresolved.

The traditional analysis assigns 爿 a phonetic role in 牀. A secondary Zhengzhang report gives a broadly similar sound comparison, but it has not been independently verified; the proposed bed object’s name or pronunciation is also unestablished.

senses.gloss: place for sitting or resting the body
senses.text: 牀 is glossed as a place for sitting or resting the body. The earliest securely dated witness for this sense is unresolved.
Bed and couch are documented meanings of 牀/床, but the earliest use of the bed word is not securely dated here.

senses.gloss: rack, support, base, or bed-like surface
senses.text: These meanings are recorded, but their dates and any path linking them to the resting-place sense are unresolved.
Classifier use is documented, but its development from another sense is not established.

limitations.text: Several meanings are documented, but the evidence does not establish when they arose or whether one developed from another, so no semantic links are asserted.
The proposed Khmer, Mon, Burmese, and Vietic comparisons do not establish a borrowing history for the Chinese word written 牀/床.

limitations.text: These images are modern digital redraws of script styles, not photographs or scans of artifacts. The bronze-style candidate is not tied to a single dated artifact, and the oracle-bone interpretation of 爿 as a bed remains uncertain; its cited use is a place name, and the inscription is not dated in the cited account.

Shuowen identifies 爿 as the sound component in 牀, but the available evidence does not independently establish its pronunciation in that role. The images alone do not prove the historical meaning or sound of either graph.
